A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 37-page work, including Appendices A–L. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish localized differences on pages 1–3; pages 4–37 are identical in extracted text and rendered appearance.

before.justification: v2 reports original LLM finetuning experiments, including safety/capability comparisons in Tables 1–2, attack evaluations and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original experimental outcomes in the main text and appendices, including benchmark comparisons, robustness results and ablations.

M1.justification: The STAR score computation and STAR-DSS loss combining cross-entropy with KL regularization are unchanged in Sections 4–5. No algorithm steps or model components change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training datasets, evaluation benchmarks and threat scenarios, including PureBad, BeaverTails, HH-RLHF, GSM8K, response adaptation, prompt poisoning and harmful prefilling.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–2 and the appendix comparisons, including SFT, RS, Vaccine, Safe LoRA, Deep Token, Safe Instruct, SEAL and LISA.

E3.justification: Model and guardrail configurations, data mixtures, metrics and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Table 6 retains the same training settings, and Appendix L retains the same safety-judging template.

E4.justification: The STAR trajectory and context-entanglement analyses, attack robustness studies, and chunk-size and KL-scaling ablations are unchanged, including Appendices C–E, J and K.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including Table 3's ± presentation for preprocessing times. Neither version adds or revises run-count, seed, uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing information relative to the other.

E6.justification: All numerical results, rankings and qualitative outcomes match, including the appendices. For example, Table 1 retains STAR-DSS safety scores of 72.12% on HEx-PHI and 89.42% on AdvBench.

T1.justification: The STAR definitions, Theorem 1's harmfulness bound, and the definitions, lemmas and full proof in Appendix A are unchanged.

C1.justification: The contributions and claims about dynamic safety shaping, theoretical safety bounds and safety/capability performance are retained. Changing 'critical safety risks' to 'important safety risks' in the abstract changes emphasis without changing scientific scope.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations of guardrail errors and context entanglement, interpretations of experimental findings, and discussions of computational cost, guardrail requirements and adversarial adaptation.

D1.justification: The code URL and availability statement, Table 6 hyperparameters, Table 3 hardware disclosure, and Appendix K implementation details are unchanged. Removing the footnote marker after the code URL does not alter the documented access information.

R1.justification: Section 8, the comparison with Deep Token in Appendix F, and the reference list are unchanged. No cited works or substantive relationships to prior research are added or removed.

P1.justification: v3 replaces 'critical' with 'important' in the abstract, removes the 'Work unrelated to Meta' footnote, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Removing the first-page footnote and its marker causes local text reflow and spacing changes across pages 1–3. Figures and tables are unchanged, and rendered pages 4–37 match exactly.

improvement.justification: The abstract adjective substitution and removal of the 'Work unrelated to Meta' footnote produce only local editorial and layout changes. The scientific argument, proofs, empirical support, reproducibility information and limitations remain unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
